title: a packet buffer was filled to its last byte and then searched with strstr
object: packet_buf, one g_malloc of packet_size + 12 bytes
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a fully-written buffer searched by a function that stops only at a terminator
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: the construct was REMOVED rather than fixed -- v4.6.8's wiretap/nettrace_3gpp_32_423.c has no g_malloc'd packet_buf at all, writing through `ws_buffer_end_ptr(&rec->data)` instead -- so the pinned code cannot carry the defect. A fix-reversal against history.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- wiretap, wsutil and ui do not use wmem, and epan/uat.c and epan/charsets.c take the crossed buffer from g_malloc or from the caller -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the buffer is written in two parts -- twelve header bytes by hand and the rest straight from the file -- so BOTH halves are accounted for and the allocation is exactly right for what is stored. What is missing is a byte for a terminator that no size calculation ever mentioned, which is why the fix adds `+1` and an explicit store rather than changing either half.
